h: The Shabbos Meals Draw Blessing Beyond the Descent of Manna

p: Now the essence of the holiness of Shabbos
"And you shall call the Shabbos a delight."
and they said, of blessed memory
(מִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה בְּרֵאשִׁית, בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה יא, ב)
for a double portion of bread came down on the sixth day;
and He sanctified it with the manna,
for none at all came down on it."
מִפְּנֵי מָה לֹא יָרַד הַמָּן בְּשַׁבָּת
why did the manna not come down on Shabbos?
as it says in the reply to that heretic!
We must also understand the matter of the blessing
surely it did not come down
was said at the time of Creation,
when the manna did not yet exist in the world!
However, one may explain the matter:
that at the conclusion of the six days of work
came the corruption of Adam HaRishon,
and it was said to him (Bereishis 3:19):
"By the sweat of your brow shall you eat bread";
that is, that he would need to toil
throughout the six days of work,
in order to refine the six attributes
כִּי שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים עָשָׂה ה׳ וְגוֹ׳
and it does not say "in six days";
the six attributes of Z'eir Anpin,
is the aspect of Malchus, the receiver.
And when the last hour arrived,
to do the labor of preparing food;
and he was also driven out of Gan Eden
שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה רַשַּׁאי לֵילֵךְ עַד שָׁם
so that he was not permitted to walk all the way there
on Shabbos to take of its fruits.
because of the doubt of Shabbos,
Who knows its times and moments
in the last moment of the sixth day,
He then radiated upon Adam HaRishon
the refinement of the six attributes of Z'eir Anpin
through the actual descent of the manna.
the holiness of Shabbos night radiated
in the meal of Chakal Tapuchin Kaddishin,
then there radiated an addition of blessing and holiness
from the dew that descends from Atika Kaddisha,
which is a very high and exalted place,
so that man cannot grasp it
for the actual descent of the manna.
And as it says in the holy Zohar (Yisro):
the head of Z'eir Anpin is filled
from the dew that descends from Atika Kaddisha,
and pours it into the Field of Holy Apples
That is, the aspect of Malchus
from a very high and exalted place,
beyond the aspect of Z'eir Anpin,
which is the refinement of the attributes,
no connection at all with a garment in this world.
וְהוּא גַּם כֵּן עִנְיַן מַתַּן תּוֹרָה
And this is also the matter of Mattan Torah:
for on Shabbos the Torah was given to Yisrael,
and the main actual giving of the Torah,
the aspect of a garment in this world,
from the dew of Atika Kaddisha.
on the Shabbos of Mattan Torah,
when He brought down on it the dew
with which He will in the future revive, etc. (Shabbos 88b);
for the aspect of the holiness of Shabbos
is a semblance of the World to Come.

p: וְהִנֵּה חֲזַ״ל לָמְדוּ ג׳ סְעוּדוֹת שַׁבָּת
Now Chazal derived the three Shabbos meals
that is mentioned in the pasuk (Shemos 16:25):
for today is a Shabbos to Hashem;
today you will not find it in the field."
which is the aspect of Malchus,
that is, the souls of Yisrael who receive.
And it is the aspect of arousal from below,
and therefore it explicitly says of it
which is a matter of arousal from below,
so that through them there be
alludes to the meal of Z'eir Anpin,
the aspect of the Name Havayah, blessed be He.
"Today you will not find it in the field"
alludes to the meal of Atika Kaddisha;
and this is the meaning of
"you will not find it in the field":
that it is without garment or hue
And in the holy Zohar too,
what is mentioned as the main one
is only the Shabbos night meal,
"even on the day of Shabbos as well."
is the aspect of arousal from below,
And one can find an allusion to this
in the words of Chazal (Bava Metzia 38a):
"A person prefers a kav of his own
to nine kavin of his fellow's."
and it is dearer to a person
that is, the nine upper levels,
that is, from the flow of Hashem Yisbarach;
as they said, of blessed memory (Shabbos 31a):
do not do to your fellow";
and Rashi explained it as referring to Hashem Yisbarach,
corresponding to the three holy Avos,
the aspect of love of kindness;
"the Torah came forth from the side of Gevurah";
However, regarding the order of the Shabbos meals,
the meal of Yitzchak is at night,
as it says in the Kisvei HaArizal.
that Avraham Avinu, peace be upon him,
that there is a Creator of all worlds;
through the aspect of love of kindness
until at the end of his days
he came to the aspect of fear,
as it was said to him (Bereishis 22:12):
that you are a God-fearing man";
and Yitzchak was born to him,
who is the root of the aspect of fear.
But we, the Children of Israel,
and it is ingrained in our nature
that Hashem Yisbarach created the world:
therefore, with us there needs to be
and after this we come to the love of kindness.
which is the aspect of accepting the Kingship of Heaven,
and from this we afterward come
שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת אִשָּׁה יִרְאַת ה׳ (מִשְׁלֵי לא, ל)
which is the aspect of "a woman who fears Hashem" (Mishlei 31:30);
וְהוּא נֶגֶד יִצְחָק אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
and it corresponds to Yitzchak Avinu, peace be upon him,
יִרְאַת ה׳ רֵאשִׁית דָּעַת (מִשְׁלֵי א, ז)
"the fear of Hashem is the beginning of knowledge" (Mishlei 1:7).
HaKadosh Baruch Hu with their own eyes."
one comes to a revelation of G-dliness perceptible to the senses;
and this is a semblance of the revelation
as they said, of blessed memory (end of Taanis):
"HaKadosh Baruch Hu will in the future
make a circle-dance for the tzaddikim
'And he will say on that day,
Behold, this is our God,'" etc.
is not yet by sensory sight,
but only through the aspect of faith.
Therefore this meal comes at night,
the hue of the garment of faith;
when there came to him a feeling
the psalm "A song for the Shabbos day" (Tehillim 92);
"To tell of Your kindness in the morning
and of Your faithfulness in the nights,"
הַמְרַמֵּז עַל קְדוּשַּׁת סְעוּדַת לֵיל שַׁבָּת
which alludes to the holiness of the Shabbos night meal.
joy is born in the heart,
"For You have gladdened me, Hashem, with Your deeds," etc.
Only, since in this world still
it is not yet in completeness;
and of the time to come it says (Yeshayahu 25:9):
"This is Hashem for Whom we hoped;
let us rejoice and be glad in His salvation"
because the revelation of G-dliness will be
perceptible to the senses, in completeness;
and therefore the joy too will be in completeness.

paragraphs.text: Source: Shabbos 89b — “… בר נחמני אמר רבי יונתן: מאי דכתיב: ״כי אתה אבינו כי אברהם לא ידענו וישראל לא יכירנו אתה ה׳ אבינו גואלנו מעולם שמך״ — לעתיד לבא יאמר לו הקדוש ברוך …” (Oz Vehadar print, p. 190) — “Apropos the Jewish people assessing their forefathers, the Gemara cites a related teaching. paragraphs.text: Source: Yeshayahu 25:9 — “ואמר ביום ההוא הנה אלהינו זה קוינו לו ויושיענו זה יהוה קוינו לו נגילה ונשמחה בישועתו” — “In that day they shall say: This is our God;We trusted in the One who delivered us. This is GOD, in whom we trusted; Let us rejoice and exult in God’s deliverance!”
